description: What an official Indian document of each kind is expected to contain, so an uploaded document can be compared against the form the law or the issuing authority asks for (app/services/formats.py). Each part is matched by looking for any of its patterns in the document text. A part that is found but sits next to an unfilled blank is reported as empty rather than present. 'why' explains, in one sentence, what the part is for and which provision asks for it. This is a checklist, not legal advice: a missing part is something to look at, not a ruling that the document is invalid.

formats.name: Rent or lease agreement
formats.authority: Registration Act 1908, Indian Stamp Act 1899, and the State's Rent Control / Tenancy Act
formats.note: A lease from year to year, for a term over one year, or reserving a yearly rent must be registered (Registration Act 1908, s. 17(1)(d)). Stamp duty and registration charges differ by State.

parts.label: Both parties named in full, with addresses
parts.why: The agreement must say who is bound by it.

parts.label: Description of the property being let
parts.why: The property must be identifiable, usually in a schedule at the end.

parts.label: Term: start date and duration
parts.why: Fixes how long the tenancy runs, which also decides whether registration is compulsory.

parts.label: Rent amount and the date it is payable
parts.why: The core obligation of the tenant.

parts.label: Security deposit and how it is refunded
parts.why: Disputes about deposits are the most common tenancy dispute; the refund terms must be written.

parts.label: Notice period for ending the tenancy
parts.why: Either side must know how much warning to give.

parts.label: Who pays maintenance, electricity and water
parts.why: Leaving this out is a frequent source of dispute.

parts.label: Permitted use of the property
parts.why: Says what the property may be used for.

parts.label: Whether subletting is allowed
parts.why: Decides whether the tenant may pass the property to someone else.

parts.label: Stamp duty / e-stamp details
parts.why: An instrument that is not duly stamped is not admissible as evidence (Indian Stamp Act 1899, s. 35).

parts.label: Registration details, where registration is compulsory
parts.why: A lease over a year must be registered (Registration Act 1908, s. 17(1)(d)); an unregistered one cannot be used to prove its terms.

parts.label: Signatures of both parties
parts.why: An unsigned agreement binds nobody.

parts.label: Two witnesses
parts.why: Two attesting witnesses are the normal practice for a registrable instrument.

parts.label: Date of the agreement
parts.why: The date decides when the term begins and the stamp duty rate that applies.

formats.name: Employment agreement or appointment letter
formats.authority: Code on Wages 2019, Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act 1946, and the State Shops and Establishments Act
formats.note: Most State Shops and Establishments Acts require an employer to give a written appointment letter stating at least the job, the wages and the hours.

parts.label: Employer and employee named in full
parts.why: Says who the contract is between.

parts.label: Job title and duties
parts.why: Fixes what the employee is engaged to do.

parts.label: Date of joining
parts.why: Service benefits and notice periods are counted from this date.

parts.label: Salary or wages, and when they are paid
parts.why: Wages must be stated; delayed or unstated wages are an offence under the Code on Wages 2019.

parts.label: Working hours
parts.why: Shops and Establishments Acts cap daily and weekly hours.

parts.label: Leave entitlement
parts.why: Statutory leave cannot be reduced by contract.

parts.label: Probation period, if any
parts.why: Probation usually carries a shorter notice period, so it must be written.

parts.label: Notice period for either side to end the employment
parts.why: Both sides must know how much warning is required.

parts.label: Place of work
parts.why: Says where the employee is required to work, and whether they can be transferred.

parts.label: Confidentiality obligation
parts.why: Protects the employer's information; should be limited to what is reasonable.

parts.label: Governing law and jurisdiction
parts.why: Decides which court hears a dispute.

parts.label: Signatures of employer and employee
parts.why: An unsigned letter is an offer, not a contract.

formats.name: Affidavit
formats.authority: Code of Civil Procedure 1908, Order XIX and s. 139
formats.note: An affidavit must be confined to facts the deponent can prove of their own knowledge, and must be verified and sworn before an authorised officer.

parts.label: Name of the court or authority it is filed before
parts.why: An affidavit is addressed to the forum it is filed in.

parts.label: Case number and the names of the parties
parts.why: Ties the affidavit to the proceeding it belongs to.

parts.label: Deponent's name, age, occupation and address
parts.why: Order XIX requires the person swearing it to be identified.

parts.label: Numbered paragraphs of facts
parts.why: Facts must be set out in numbered paragraphs, each confined to what the deponent knows.

parts.label: Verification clause
patterns: true to the best of my knowledge
parts.why: Section 139 CPC requires the deponent to verify which paragraphs are true to knowledge and which to belief.

parts.label: Place and date of swearing
parts.why: An affidavit must show where and when it was sworn.

parts.label: Signature of the deponent
parts.why: The deponent signs below the verification.

parts.label: Attestation by a notary or oath commissioner
parts.why: An affidavit that was not sworn before an authorised officer has no value.

formats.name: RTI application
formats.note: Section 6(2): the applicant need not give any reason for the request, or any personal details beyond what is needed to contact them.

parts.label: Addressed to the Public Information Officer
parts.why: Section 6(1) requires the request to be made to the PIO of the public authority.

parts.label: Name of the public authority
parts.why: Says which body holds the information.

parts.label: Subject line: request for information under the RTI Act
parts.why: Identifies the application as an RTI request rather than an ordinary letter.

parts.label: The information asked for, clearly listed
parts.why: The request must be specific enough for the PIO to identify the records.

parts.label: Period the information relates to
parts.why: Narrowing the period avoids a rejection for being too vague.

parts.label: Application fee and how it was paid
parts.why: Section 6(1) requires the prescribed fee; the Central fee is ₹10, and an applicant below the poverty line pays nothing.

parts.label: Applicant's name and full postal address
parts.why: Section 6(2) allows the authority to ask only for the contact details needed to reply.

parts.label: Declaration that the applicant is an Indian citizen
parts.why: The right under s. 3 belongs to citizens, so many forms ask for this declaration.

parts.label: Signature, place and date
parts.why: A written request must be signed and dated.

formats.name: Legal notice
formats.authority: General practice; for a dishonoured cheque, Negotiable Instruments Act 1881, s. 138(b)
formats.note: For a cheque bounce the notice must be sent within 30 days of the bank's memo and must demand payment within 15 days.

parts.label: Sender or their advocate, with address
parts.why: The recipient must know who the notice is from and where to reply.

parts.label: Recipient's name and address
parts.why: A notice served on the wrong address is no notice.

parts.label: Subject line
parts.why: States in one line what the notice is about.

parts.label: The facts, in numbered paragraphs
parts.why: Sets out what happened, so the recipient can answer it.

parts.label: What is demanded, and by when
parts.why: A notice without a clear demand and deadline cannot be acted on.

parts.label: What follows if the demand is not met
parts.why: Warns the recipient of the step the sender will take next.

parts.label: Signature and date
parts.why: The date starts the clock on the deadline in the notice.

formats.name: Sale deed for immovable property
formats.authority: Transfer of Property Act 1882, s. 54; Registration Act 1908, s. 17; Indian Stamp Act 1899
formats.note: A sale of immovable property worth ₹100 or more can be made only by a registered instrument (Transfer of Property Act 1882, s. 54).

parts.label: Seller and buyer named in full, with addresses
parts.why: Identifies who is transferring the property and to whom.

parts.label: How the seller came to own the property
parts.why: Shows the chain of title the buyer is relying on.

parts.label: Sale price and how it was paid
parts.why: Sale requires a price paid or promised (Transfer of Property Act 1882, s. 54).

parts.label: Schedule of the property with boundaries and area
parts.why: The property must be described precisely enough to be identified on the ground.

parts.label: Delivery of possession
parts.why: Records when the buyer takes the property.

parts.label: Declaration that the property is free of loans and claims
parts.why: The buyer needs the seller's assurance that no lender or claimant has a right over it.

parts.label: Indemnity by the seller
parts.why: Gives the buyer a remedy if the title turns out to be defective.

parts.label: Stamp duty paid
parts.why: Stamp duty is payable on the market value; an unstamped deed is inadmissible (Indian Stamp Act 1899, s. 35).

parts.label: Registration before the Sub-Registrar
parts.why: An unregistered sale deed does not transfer ownership (Registration Act 1908, s. 17).

parts.label: Two attesting witnesses
parts.why: Two witnesses must attest the execution.

parts.label: Signatures of seller and buyer
parts.why: Both sides must execute the deed.

formats.name: Act of Parliament as published
formats.authority: The form in which Central Acts are published in the Gazette of India and on India Code
formats.note: This checks the published structure of an Act, not its contents. A missing part usually means the copy is an extract rather than the full Act.

parts.label: Short title with the Act number and year
parts.why: Every Act carries an official number and year, e.g. "ACT NO. 35 OF 2019".

parts.label: Long title: what the Act is for
parts.why: The long title states the purpose and is used to interpret the Act.

parts.label: Enacting formula
patterns: be it enacted by the legislature
year of the republic of india
parts.why: The words by which Parliament enacts the law.

parts.label: Extent and commencement section
patterns: extends to the whole of india
parts.why: Says where the Act applies and from when.

parts.label: Definitions section
patterns: in this act, unless the context otherwise requires
parts.why: Defines the terms the rest of the Act uses.

parts.label: Arrangement of sections (table of contents)
parts.why: Published Acts carry a table of sections at the front.

parts.label: Chapters and numbered sections
parts.why: The body of the Act.

parts.label: Offences and penalties
parts.why: Most regulatory Acts set out what happens when they are broken.

parts.label: Power to make rules
parts.why: Delegates the detail to rules made by the government.

parts.label: Schedules
parts.why: Schedules carry forms, lists and rates referred to in the sections.
